plan: Second-price auctions reward truthful bidding: your bid determines if you win, not what you pay (you pay the second-highest bid). To maximize expected profit, bid exactly your private value—this sets the correct cutoff where winning is profitable and avoids overpaying if others bid between your value and an inflated bid. With no informative history and one round only, there’s no strategic benefit to shading or bluffing. Therefore, set the bid equal to my value, $25, as my maximum willingness to pay.

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the weakly dominant strategy is truthful bidding. Bidding my value ensures I win precisely when the second-highest competing bid is below my value, and I pay that second-highest price, maximizing expected profit. No history to exploit; one round only. My value is 18, so I bid 18 to capture all profitable wins. ]

In a 3-bidder second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. It maximizes expected profit because your bid only determines whether you win, not the price you pay (the second-highest bid). With one round and $0.1 increments, there’s no benefit to shading or overbidding. Overbidding risks negative profit; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. I will bid my value exactly and accept tie-breaking randomness.
